requirements.requirement: The product must show a handoff card for the matched office that carries eight fields: office name with a one-line plain-language description, exact building and room, a map, the office website, hours, phone number, what to say on arrival or by phone, and the specific next step.
done_when: A tester submits a question that matches one service area in Appendix A and sees a card with all eight fields populated.
A tester opens the card for every office listed in Appendix A and finds no empty field.
A tester follows the website link and dials the phone number on a sample of cards and reaches the office named on the card.

requirements.requirement: The product must show the location and map for the campus the student attends, Main or North, when an office exists on both.
done_when: A tester identified as a North Campus student sees the North building and room for an office that exists on both campuses.
The same question from a tester identified as a Main Campus student shows the Main building and room.
The map link on each card opens to the single building named on the card, not a general campus map.

requirements.requirement: The student must be able to ask a question and receive a handoff card without a login, a name, an account, or any identifier.
done_when: A tester opens the standalone page in a private browser window and reaches the question field with no sign-in step.
A tester completes a full exchange and is never asked for a name, email address, MEID, or student number.
A tester inspects every form field in the student interface and finds none that requests identity.

requirements.requirement: The product must acknowledge what the student said in plain human language before it names an office or shows a card.
done_when: A tester submits a question that expresses distress and the first sentence of the reply is an acknowledgment, with the office name appearing only after it.
A tester reviews the replies to the full test set and finds no reply that opens with an office name, a label, or a form.

requirements.requirement: The product must reply in the language the student wrote or spoke in.
done_when: A tester submits the same question in English, Spanish, Arabic, Vietnamese, and Tagalog and each reply is in the language of the question.
The handoff card text, apart from proper names, addresses, and phone numbers, appears in the same language as the reply.
No translate button or language picker is needed to receive the reply in that language.

requirements.requirement: The student must be able to speak a question and hear the reply read aloud in the same language, using the browser Web Speech API.
done_when: A tester on a browser that supports the Web Speech API speaks a question in Spanish and sees it transcribed into the question field.
The tester hears the reply read aloud in Spanish.
A tester watching network traffic during voice use sees no audio sent to any server.
A tester on a browser without Web Speech API support can still type a question and read the reply.

requirements.requirement: The student must be able to complete the full exchange, from question to handoff card, on a phone.
done_when: A tester on a phone-width screen submits a question and reads the whole card with no horizontal scrolling.
Every link and the phone number on the card can be tapped on a phone, and the phone number opens the dialer.

requirements.requirement: The product must answer directly, in plain language, when the responsible department has supplied a current answer to the question (Tier 1).
done_when: A tester asks each Tier 1 example in the PRD (tutoring hours, food pantry location, last day to withdraw, how to request a transcript) and receives the stored department answer.
The facts in each reply match the department-supplied answer held in the system prompt, with nothing added.
A tester asks a question for which no department answer is stored and receives a handoff to a person, not a composed answer.

requirements.requirement: The product must give the general answer and then present the phone number, scheduling link, and walk-in location when the student’s specifics need a person (Tier 2).
done_when: A tester asks each Tier 2 example in the PRD (aid impact of dropping a class, requesting accommodations, where to start on transferring) and receives a general answer followed by the path to a person.
The path shown includes a phone number, a scheduling link, and a walk-in location for the responsible office.
The reply does not state an outcome for the student’s individual case.

requirements.requirement: The product must route crisis and Title IX messages straight to a person through hard-coded routing that runs ahead of all other routing, with no answer attempted (Tier 3).
done_when: A tester submits a message stating self-harm or an immediate safety risk and the first reply shows 911, 988, and Counseling.
A tester submits a message that raises a Title IX matter indirectly and the Title IX Coordinator card appears in the first reply.
A tester submits a message that combines a crisis statement with a routine question and the crisis routing appears first.
In every Tier 3 test the reply contains no attempted answer to the underlying problem.

requirements.requirement: The product must open a card for each responsible office when one message describes a situation that involves more than one office.
done_when: A tester submits a message that states failing a class and an aid hold, and cards for both advising and financial aid appear in one reply.
Each card carries its own what-to-say line that reflects the student’s situation.
The tester is not asked to restate the situation to receive the second card.

requirements.requirement: The product must never name a course, and must link the published program checksheet from the fixed lookup table and send first-semester students to an advisor before they register.
done_when: A tester asks which classes to take for a named program and the reply contains no course code or course title.
The checksheet link in the reply matches the address stored for that program in the JavaScript lookup table.
A tester who states that this is a first semester receives an advisor prompt in the reply.
A tester reviews the replies to the full test set and finds no link that is absent from the lookup table or the verified service links.

requirements.requirement: Each service office must be able to confirm, correct, and add answers in its own words through the staff knowledge builder and the question intake form, which contain no AI.
done_when: A staff tester opens the staff knowledge builder and the question intake form and can enter a confirmation, a correction, and a new answer for the office.
A submitted entry is stored and can be retrieved by the content maintainer.
A tester watching network traffic while using either form sees no call to an AI model.
A corrected answer appears in student replies within the turnaround the author sets.

requirements.requirement: The product must send nothing from the browser except the text of the student’s question and receive nothing except the reply.
done_when: A tester watching network traffic during a full exchange sees the question text as the only student-originated content in any request.
No request carries a name, email address, MEID, student record, or persistent identifier.
A tester finds no cookie or browser storage entry that identifies the student after the session.

requirements.requirement: The product must log only anonymous routing counts, namely which cards were shown, the detected language, and success or error.
done_when: A tester submits a question and the log entry holds the card names, the detected language, and a success or error flag.
The log entry holds no question text, no reply text, and no free-text field.
A tester reviewing the log after the full test set cannot link any entry to a person or a device.

requirements.requirement: The student must be able to give an optional thumbs up or thumbs down after a handoff card, with no identifying data attached.
done_when: A thumbs up and thumbs down control appears after a handoff card.
A tester can leave the card without responding and nothing is blocked.
The stored response holds only the rating and the card it refers to.

requirements.requirement: The product must make its AI call through one stateless server-side function that holds the credential in a secrets manager and adds the system prompt.
done_when: A tester searching the page source and browser storage finds no API credential.
A tester searching the page source and network responses finds no system prompt text.
A student tester completes an exchange without supplying a credential.
A second request to the function shows no knowledge of the first.

requirements.requirement: The product must run as a standalone page and as an embeddable widget from one codebase with the same prompt and the same cards.
done_when: A tester asks the same question on the standalone page and in the embedded widget and receives the same routing and the same card content.
A change to one card, deployed once, appears in both the standalone page and the widget.
The widget loads inside an existing services page without that page changing its own code beyond the embed.

requirements.requirement: The product must make every AI call through a single request function so that a change of provider alters only the endpoint, the authorization header, and the response parsing.
done_when: A code reviewer finds exactly one function that calls the AI provider.
A developer points that function at a second provider by editing only the endpoint, the authorization header, and the response parsing.
After the change, the full test set is re-run and the routing results are recorded against the results from the first provider.

requirements.requirement: The product must meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA before any live release.
done_when: A WCAG 2.1 Level AA audit of the standalone page and the widget is complete and its report is on file.
Every issue the audit marks as blocking is resolved and retested.
A tester completes a full exchange using only a keyboard and again using a screen reader.

out_of_scope: Collecting student data or requiring a login, a name, an account, or a student record.
Answers authored by the model; every answer is written and owned by the staff of the responsible office.
Naming courses or building links with AI; the product links only the published program checksheet from a fixed lookup table.
A live connection to a person from the handoff card; the PRD places this in version 2.
Attempting an answer for crisis, Title IX, or other Tier 3 situations; these go to a person at once.
Use of a translation service, and sending audio off the device.
Retaining student conversations to train a model, and logging question text, reply text, or any free-text field.
Extension to additional offices or other Maricopa colleges before the pilot passes its thresholds, and redesign during the pilot semester.

questions: Where does the pilot run: inside the program Discord, on the standalone page, or both? If Discord, which of the stated requirements still apply there (no login, voice, campus-aware cards, the embeddable widget)?
Who hosts the server-side function and whose AI credential does it use for the pilot, given that the district model instance and district GitHub account are not yet live?
How does a submission from the staff knowledge builder or question intake form reach the system prompt: where is it stored, who reviews it, and how soon must it appear in student replies?
How does the product learn whether a student attends Main or North: does it ask, or is it inferred from the message?
What are the pass numbers for routing confirmed correct and for questions with no service match, and where are the anonymous routing counts and thumbs results stored?

requirements.area: How it works: intake and parsing
requirements.requirement: The user can drop a Canvas Common Cartridge export (.imscc) into the page and choose which checks to run.
done_when: A tester drops a valid .imscc file onto the page and sees the list of checks available to select.
The tester selects a subset of checks and the report contains findings from the selected checks only.
The tester runs the tool on exports with outcomes absent, outcomes present and unbound, and outcomes bound, and a report is produced in all three cases.

requirements.requirement: The product reports every finding with the standard it comes from, the location in the course where it is fixed, and the figures that produced it.
done_when: Every finding in the report shows a standard reference, a course location and the counts or values behind it.
A check whose input is missing from the package produces no finding and no pass result for that check.
No standard is shown as satisfied unless a check verified it in the package.

requirements.requirement: The product reports Canvas setup (outcome objects, rubric bindings, assignment groups and the weighting scheme) as one task with an ordered sequence of steps.
done_when: On a course with several setup gaps, the report shows one Canvas setup task and not separate defects.
The task lists its steps in a stated order covering outcomes, rubric bindings, assignment groups and weighting.

requirements.requirement: The product presents outcome to assessment alignment as a matrix and resolves each course competency to the assignment and rubric criterion that assess it.
done_when: On an export with bound outcomes, the report shows a matrix of outcomes against graded items.
Each competency is listed with the assignment and criterion that assess it, or is flagged as having none.
On an export with no outcomes file, the alignment check does not fire and the seat hours and objectives checks still run.

requirements.requirement: The product tests each objective against a verb bank and proposes an observable replacement verb at the appropriate level of Bloom's Taxonomy.
done_when: An objective using a verb outside the bank is flagged against OSCQR 9.
Each flagged objective is shown with at least one proposed replacement verb and its taxonomy level.
An objective that already uses an observable verb from the bank is not flagged.

requirements.requirement: The product estimates student hours for the course content, reconciles them against the outside-work allowance entered by the instructor, and writes the confirmed figure into each module overview.
done_when: The tester is asked for the outside-work allowance and the tool shows total student hours as credits multiplied by forty.
The report shows an hours estimate for every graded item, reading page and video, with totals compared to the allowance at module level and course level.
The tester changes an estimate and the module and course totals update.
After approval and export, each module overview in the package contains the confirmed hours figure.

requirements.area: Assessment validity and the AI resistance audit
requirements.requirement: The product flags a graded item as a construct validity finding only when it is both completable by a generative model within sixty seconds and at or above the median point value of graded items in the course.
done_when: An item that meets both conditions appears as a finding worded as a threat to construct validity, not as academic integrity.
An item that meets only one of the two conditions does not appear as a finding.
The finding shows the item point value and the course median used for the comparison.

requirements.area: Assessment validity and the AI resistance audit
requirements.requirement: The product reads the rubric criteria of every graded item and reports which of the seven kinds of process evidence each one collects, with a band of strong, adequate or exposed.
done_when: Each measured assessment is listed with the kinds of process evidence found in its rubric criteria and one of the three bands.
Each measured assessment is returned with two or three specific additions.
Low-stakes items are listed separately and carry no band.
Changing an assignment title without changing its rubric does not change the result.

requirements.requirement: The product checks the package against the OSCQR groups for course overview and information, technology and support, interaction, and assessment and feedback.
done_when: The report contains a section for each of the four groups, with each finding naming its OSCQR standard number.
Course information that is absent from the Canvas pages in the export is reported as not found.
A standard in these groups that cannot be verified from the file appears in the human review list and not as a pass.

requirements.area: Accessibility, and the boundary of what a parser can see
requirements.requirement: The product verifies alternative text on images, descriptive link text, header cells on tables, typeface, and the presence of captions on video, and counts PDF files without opening them.
done_when: A package containing an image without alternative text, a link with non-descriptive text and a table without header cells produces one finding for each, with its location.
A typeface departure is reported against OSCQR 23 and is not labelled an accessibility defect.
The report states the number of PDF files and directs the instructor to YuJa Panorama for them.
The report states that caption accuracy was not verified.

requirements.requirement: The product counts the distinct typefaces, sizes and colours in the course and applies a palette chosen by the instructor as inline styles, refusing any colour pair that fails WCAG AA contrast.
done_when: The report shows the number of distinct typefaces, sizes and colours found.
The tester selects a palette with a failing colour pair and the tool does not allow it to be applied.
After a passing palette is applied and exported, the page content carries inline style attributes and no style block or class-based styling.

requirements.requirement: The product flags any date that carries more than two deadlines and any graded item that has no due date.
done_when: A course with three items due on one date shows a finding naming that date and the items.
A graded item with no due date is flagged, with a note that it appears in neither the student To Do list nor the calendar.
A date with two deadlines is not flagged.

requirements.requirement: The product scans the filenames and file types in course Files, flags candidates that may hold student data, and never deletes a file.
done_when: A package whose Files area contains a gradebook spreadsheet or roster shows that file as a flagged candidate.
After export, every flagged file is still present in the package.
The scan result is based on filename and type only, and the report says so.

requirements.requirement: The product writes only the changes the instructor approved into the package, repackages it for reimport, and lists the tasks that must be done by hand in Canvas.
done_when: A change the tester did not approve is absent from the exported package.
The exported package has the same file count as the original and all XML files are byte-identical.
The exported package imports into Canvas and every approved change is visible after the editor saves the page.
After export, the tool shows a short list of the remaining tasks that only Canvas can perform.

requirements.area: Not scored, enumerated for human review
requirements.requirement: The product lists each standard that cannot be verified from a file, with the reason a parser cannot evaluate it, the established method for evaluating it, and a checkbox that is unchecked by default.
done_when: Each listed standard shows a reason, a method and a checkbox, and none of them carries a score.
On first use every checkbox is unchecked.
The tester checks a box, closes the browser, reopens the tool on the same machine and sees the box still checked.

requirements.requirement: The product processes the course package entirely in the browser tab and stores nothing except the human review checkboxes.
done_when: With the browser network panel open during a full run and export, no request carries course content.
The tool runs with no sign-in and no account.
After a run, browser storage for the page holds the checkbox states and no course content.

requirements.requirement: The product is delivered as one static HTML file whose only external dependency is JSZip, and it runs from disk, from static web hosting, and from a Canvas course as a linked or embedded file.
done_when: The file opened from disk completes a full run and export.
The file uploaded to Canvas course Files and linked or embedded in a page completes a full run with instructor rights only.
With JSZip placed beside the file and the script tag repointed, the tool completes a full run with no request to a third-party script source.
A tester can reach and operate every disclosure control by keyboard, and text contrast meets WCAG AA.

requirements.requirement: The product composes a prompt that contains only the flagged passages, and the user pastes it into the sanctioned model and pastes the reply back into the tool.
done_when: The composed prompt contains the flagged assignment prompt and its rubric criteria and no other course content.
With the network panel open, no request to a model originates from the page.
The pasted reply appears as an editable draft that the tester can approve, edit or discard.
A discarded draft makes no change to the exported package.

requirements.requirement: The product proposes two or three substitute assessments for each flagged item, at equivalent cognitive demand, chosen from the reference library by finding type and by the evidence the rubric criteria show.
done_when: Each flagged item shows two or three proposed substitutions.
Each substitution can be traced to an entry in the reference library.
The same package run twice selects the same reference entries for the same finding.
No proposal is described as an essay a model cannot write or as a detector.

requirements.requirement: The product holds its reference library as versioned files beside the tool and never calls a scholarly index while running.
done_when: The library files are present beside the tool and carry a version.
With the network panel open during a run, no request goes to an external index.
Each library entry carries a citation.

requirements.requirement: The product flags content offered in a single modality, assignments that accept one submission format, and modules with no learner choice, self-assessment or activation of prior knowledge, and proposes a specific addition for each.
done_when: A module whose content exists in one modality is flagged with a proposed second modality.
An assignment accepting one submission format is flagged with a proposed alternative means of expression.
The report states how Universal Design for Learning differs from accessibility.

requirements.requirement: The product generates an editable interaction plan and Regular and Substantive Interaction statement and checks the draft against the OSCQR interaction standards and the two-of-five substantive interaction test.
done_when: The draft contains a weekly teaching announcement, a feedback schedule, a facilitated discussion, a response-time commitment and a monitoring and outreach policy.
The tester can edit the draft before copying it.
The tool shows which of the five substantive interaction activities the draft covers and whether at least two are met.

requirements.requirement: The user can select an instructional design model and see the same findings reworded through that model.
done_when: Selecting a lens changes the wording or grouping of the report.
The number and identity of findings are the same before and after a lens is selected.
Clearing the selection returns the report to its default form.

requirements.requirement: The user can enter course objectives, lesson objectives and a topic, and the product returns a starter course package to import.
done_when: With only objectives and a topic entered, and no file loaded, the tool returns a module outline with a stated time cost.
The scaffold shows an assessment matched to each objective, an interaction plan and Universal Design for Learning options.
The module time costs sum to no more than the seat hour budget.
The starter package imports into Canvas.

requirements.area: Version 2: one tool, four front doors, and export formats
requirements.requirement: The product presents Audit, Builder, Syllabus and Report as tabs over one tool, and the user can export the report as standalone HTML, as PDF and as a Word file in addition to the Canvas cartridge.
done_when: The four tabs are present and each opens its named function.
A seat hour figure confirmed in one tab appears in the Syllabus tab without retyping.
The exported HTML report opens offline with its styling intact.
The Canvas cartridge export remains available and unchanged.

requirements.requirement: The product can send flagged passages to a server-side endpoint that holds the institutional credential and authenticates the user through single sign-on.
done_when: The page source and browser storage contain no credential.
A user who is not signed in through single sign-on receives no generated text.
The request body contains flagged passages only, and the response contains generated text only.
Changing the model requires a change to one endpoint and one request shape, with no change to the checks.

out_of_scope: Batch analysis across many courses, because that reports to an institution and not to an instructor.
Comparison of an online section against its in-person master course.
Reporting results to an accreditation office, an assessment office or any administrator.
Student engagement monitoring or any feature that needs continuous student data.
Certifying a course or submitting a score; the product reports to the instructor only.
Opening or remediating PDF files; the product counts them and refers the instructor to the tool the district already licenses.
Verifying caption accuracy; the product confirms only that captions are present.
Deleting instructor files or making any change to the package without instructor approval.

questions: What are the nineteen checks by name, and what is the exact pass or fail rule for each, including the OSCQR group checks that section 4 names without rules?
Which version 2 features exist in the preview today, and which of them are in scope for the next build?
Which changes does version 1 write into the package on approval, and how does that list fit the rule that all XML stays byte-identical?
Which rules produce the seat hour estimate: the hours per page of reading, the assumed video duration, and the conversion from point weight to hours?
Is the human review list ten standards or twenty-three, and which standards are on it?

requirements.requirement: The product must open on a resources hub that shows the classified news feed, resource cards, a progress bar, and a link into the growth plan.
done_when: Opening the hub displays the news feed, the resource cards and the progress bar on one page with no search needed.
Selecting the growth plan link opens the growth plan page.
The hub loads when its address is opened directly, without first visiting another page.

requirements.requirement: The product must show the growth plan as a priority roadmap in which each item has a target date, a checkbox and a deadline badge.
done_when: Every roadmap item displays a target date, a checkbox and a deadline badge.
Items appear in priority order as defined in the plan content.
The deadline badge on an item reflects that item's target date when the page is opened on a later day.

requirements.requirement: The product must keep checkbox states and notes in the browser's localStorage on the user's own device.
done_when: A checkbox that is checked remains checked after the page is closed and reopened in the same browser.
A note that is entered is still present after the page is closed and reopened in the same browser.
The checkbox states and notes are visible as entries in the browser's localStorage for the site.

requirements.requirement: The product must add an entry to the activity log automatically when the user checks off a task, with a category badge on the entry.
done_when: Checking off a task in the growth plan creates a new activity log entry with no further action by the user.
The new entry displays a category badge.
The entry is still in the activity log after the page is closed and reopened in the same browser.

requirements.requirement: The user must be able to export the activity log as a CSV file.
done_when: Selecting the export control downloads a file in CSV format.
The file contains one row for each entry shown in the activity log.
The file opens in a spreadsheet application with each field in its own column.

requirements.requirement: The product must provide a UX toolkit page that presents a reference of design tools, vocabulary and practice projects.
done_when: The page shows three groups of content: design tools, vocabulary and practice projects.
The page loads when its address is opened directly.
The page uses the same header and navigation as the other pages.

requirements.requirement: The product must provide a conference page that holds one working proposal with its abstract, learning outcomes and preparation list, and shows the proposal deadline.
done_when: The page displays an abstract, a set of learning outcomes and a preparation list for a single proposal.
The proposal deadline is visible on the page without scrolling through the proposal text to find it.
The page loads when its address is opened directly.

requirements.requirement: The user must be able to copy the project context block to the clipboard with one tap.
done_when: One tap on the copy control places the full text of the context block on the clipboard.
Pasting into another application reproduces the context block text exactly.
The copy works on the intended iPad and on a laptop browser.

requirements.requirement: The product must fetch its curated pool of RSS sources each time the page is opened, with no schedule or background job.
done_when: With a connection, opening the page triggers a fetch for the RSS sources, visible in the browser network inspector.
Reopening the page triggers the fetch again.
No fetch occurs while the page is closed, and the build contains no scheduled task, server job or background worker that fetches feeds.

requirements.requirement: The product must route each fetched item to a feed tab using a keyword classifier and no AI model.
done_when: An item whose text contains a keyword assigned to a tab appears under that tab.
The same item is routed to the same tab on every fetch.
The browser network inspector shows no request to an AI model service while the feed is fetched and classified.

requirements.requirement: The product must send each RSS fetch through three public cross-origin proxies in sequence and skip a source silently when all three fail.
done_when: When the first proxy is blocked, the same source is requested through the second proxy, and then through the third if the second is blocked.
When all three proxies are blocked for one source, the items from the other sources still display.
A skipped source produces no error message, alert or broken layout on the page.

requirements.requirement: The product must cache the fetched feed locally for 24 hours so that it stays readable with no connection.
done_when: After one successful fetch, opening the page with the device offline displays the previously fetched items under their tabs.
The cached items are present in the browser's local storage for the site.
Opening the page offline shows no error in place of the feed while the cache is less than 24 hours old.

requirements.requirement: The product must run with no account, no analytics and no transmission of user data.
done_when: Every page is usable with no sign-in or account prompt from the product itself.
The source contains no analytics or tracking script.
With the network inspector open, checking a task, writing a note and exporting the log send no request that contains user data.

requirements.requirement: The product must be delivered as six linked static HTML pages that share one design system, one header and one navigation pattern, with no backend and no build step.
done_when: The published files run from static hosting with no server code and no compile or bundling step.
The header and navigation are identical on all pages, and each navigation link opens its page.
Each page loads and displays correctly when opened directly by its own address.

requirements.requirement: The product must remain usable offline on the intended iPad, including its locally saved documents and videos.
done_when: With the iPad offline, each page opens and the growth plan, activity log and context block work.
With the iPad offline, links to documents and videos saved on that iPad open.

requirements.requirement: The product must present a request form that asks the six problem-first questions: what the office is trying to get done, what is getting in the way, how the work is done today, who does the work and who is affected and who approves a change, how often it happens and how long it takes, and what better would look like.

A completed form can be submitted and the submitted answers match what was typed, question by question.
requirements.status: Drafted, with the domain for review

requirements.requirement: The product must offer an optional kind of help field with five choices: a tool, an agentic workflow, training, a look at the process, or not sure.

A form submitted with no choice selected is accepted and saved.
A form submitted with a choice selected shows that choice on the saved request.
requirements.status: Drafted, with the domain for review

requirements.requirement: The user must be able to answer any question with I do not know and still submit the form without help.
done_when: A form with I do not know entered in every one of the six questions is accepted and saved.
The form shows no error or warning that treats I do not know as an invalid answer.
A staff member who has not seen the form before completes and submits it with no assistance in an observed test, and the time taken is recorded.

requirements.requirement: The product must save each submitted request and show it in the list of requests received with the status new.
done_when: Immediately after submission, the request appears in the list of requests received.
The request is shown with the status new.
The request is still in the list after the page is closed and reopened in the same browser.
requirements.status: Drafted, with the domain for review

requirements.requirement: The product must hold an inventory in which each reported tool or automated workflow is logged with its college, category, license, and how it is reported to be working.
done_when: The inventory screen lists three records in the working draft.
Each record displays a value for college, category, license, and how it is reported to be working.
Each of the three records can be traced to a real report supplied by the author, and none is sample data.
requirements.status: Drafted, with the domain for review

requirements.requirement: The product must let a domain member close each inventory record with one of five answers: share across colleges, consolidate to a district license, replace with something built, retire, or leave as is.
done_when: An inventory record offers exactly the five answers named in the PRD.
Only one answer can be recorded on a record at a time.
The recorded answer is displayed on the inventory record after saving.

requirements.requirement: The product must let a domain member close each request with one of four answers: pilot, discovery, not an AI problem, or declined.
done_when: A request offers exactly the four answers named in the PRD.
Recording an answer changes the request status from new to that answer in the list of requests received.
A request recorded as not an AI problem also records the owner it was routed to.

requirements.requirement: The product must keep the request track closed to live requests until the inventory has been published.
done_when: Before the inventory is published, the request form is not offered to college staff as a live intake.
After the inventory is published, the request form is available to student services staff and leaders at the ten colleges.
The date the inventory was published and the date the request track opened are both recorded.

requirements.requirement: The product must let a domain member record an assessment of an entry against the six dimensions: student impact, staff time returned, readiness, risk, feasibility, and scale.
done_when: An assessment record has one entry field for each of the six dimensions, labeled with the names used in the PRD.
A saved assessment is attached to its request or inventory record and can be reopened and read.
The assessment record displays no computed total, rank or formula result, consistent with the PRD statement that the dimensions are a conversation structure and not a formula.

requirements.requirement: The product must check each proposed tool for privacy, security and accessibility as three pass or fail gates before any assessment against the dimensions is recorded.
done_when: Each proposed tool has three separate gate results, each recorded as pass or fail.
An assessment against the six dimensions cannot be saved until all three gates are recorded.
A tool that fails any one gate is marked as not proceeding and receives no assessment against the dimensions.

requirements.requirement: The product must require a written reason whenever an answer is recorded on a request or an inventory record.
done_when: An answer cannot be saved while the reason field is empty.
The saved reason is displayed next to the answer on the entry.
The same rule applies to a declined request as to a pilot.

requirements.requirement: The product must provide a decision log that lists every assessed entry with its answer and the written reason.
done_when: Every entry that has an answer appears in the decision log, and no entry without an answer appears.
Each row shows the entry, the answer and the reason.
Declined entries appear in the same list and with the same fields as approved entries, with no filter that hides them by default.

requirements.requirement: The product must provide a dashboard that shows college coverage, products duplicated across colleges, how tools are licensed, and what kinds of tools exist.
done_when: The dashboard shows which of the ten colleges have at least one inventory record and which have none.
A product logged at more than one college is shown once with the colleges that reported it.
The dashboard shows a count of inventory records by license and a count by category, and each count matches the inventory.

requirements.requirement: The product must collect no student data and must save a prototype submission only in the browser of the person who submitted it.
done_when: No form field asks for a student name, student identifier or student record.
With the browser network inspector open, submitting the form sends no request that contains the submitted answers.
A request submitted in one browser does not appear in the list of requests received when the product is opened in a different browser or on a different device.
requirements.status: Drafted, with the domain for review

requirements.requirement: The product must have sign-in, access control and an audit trail before it is launched or holds staff names, departments and decisions.
done_when: A person who is not signed in cannot view submitted requests, assessments or decisions.
Only members of the domain can record an assessment or an answer.
Every recorded assessment and answer is logged with who made it and when, and the log cannot be edited from the product.

requirements.requirement: The product must run as one self-contained HTML file written in vanilla JavaScript, with no framework, no backend, no account, no AI model and no API key.
done_when: The published product is a single HTML file that loads and works with no other script, stylesheet or library file requested.
The source contains no call to an AI model service and no API key.
The file opens from its GitHub Pages address and displays correctly in both the light theme and the dark theme.
requirements.status: Drafted, with the domain for review

The lock state is unchanged after the page is reloaded.

Every data-entry section reached from the home view opens with written directions above its first field.

The diagnosis appears without the student copying a prompt into an AI tool.
An optional deeper dive hands the student a prompt to run in their own AI account.

After the last question, a single goals statement containing the student’s answers is shown and saved.
The student can record one reach job, and that job is shown as the anchor on the launch plan.

The links hub accepts and saves LinkedIn, Behance, portfolio, reel, Instagram and GitHub links.
The profile has no field for a last name, email, student ID, address or phone number.

The status can be changed to applied, interview, and offer or pass, and the change remains after a reload.
Opening the entry shows the description, the resume edits and the cover letter together.

The row holds only the date, employer name, job title, job URL, interest level and program area.
At the moment of saving, the student sees a notice stating what is sent to Career Services and why.
Saving a freelance client entry adds no row.

requirements.area: Job log, base materials, tailoring, and critical AI review

The pasted reply is saved with the client entry and is still there after a reload.

With a base resume but no base cover letter, the Tailor flow does not run and states that a hand-written cover letter is required.
With both saved, the Tailor flow opens.

requirements.area: Job log, base materials, tailoring, and critical AI review

A reflection field accepts and saves what the student edited.

The pull-gaps step uses no more than 6 saved job descriptions and adds the returned skills to the same list.

The connection request step asks for a LinkedIn message under 300 characters and offers a redraft for the same contact.

The set contains an opener, a behavioral (STAR) question, a situational question, a competency-based question and a closing question, each labeled by type.
Two saved jobs with different descriptions produce different questions.
A job with no description entered produces no questions and a message asking for the description.

No coaching reply contains a full model answer or a rewritten version of the student’s answer.
The agent file states the rule against writing the answer in its rules part.

requirements.area: Launch plan and career agent, the capstone export

done_when: The 90-day plan lists gaps taken from the student’s saved jobs, each with a named low-cost resource.
The weekly schedule covers Monday through Sunday in time blocks and includes a Sunday review block.
Changing the committed hours and running the step again changes the schedule.

requirements.requirement: Render must let the student download a package they own that opens with no login and no connection to Canvas.
done_when: The exported dashboard opens in a browser on a device that has never opened Render, with no sign-in.
The exported dashboard offers four color themes.
The package contains the job tracker, the tailored documents filed with their job descriptions, and the agent files with a readme.
The student can run the export at any point in the semester, not only in week 15.

requirements.requirement: Render must assemble an AI mentor agent file that states it is an AI and asks about a human mentor at every check-in.
done_when: The assembled file says in plain words that the mentor is an AI.
The student can record a human mentor so far, and that line appears in every update copied for the AI mentor.
Every later workshop step ends with a button that copies an update built from the current jobs, panel results and gap list.
The file’s rules tell the agent to end every reply with one thing to do this week and never to invent a person, a group or a course.

requirements.requirement: Render must assemble a job search agent file from the student’s goal, strengths, resume, and where to look and what to skip.

The file instructs the agent to confirm each opening is still posted on the employer’s own careers page before listing it.
When the student pastes the reply back, the openings can be added to the job log.

Each job carries four panel members whose names and titles the student can edit.
The pasted reply shows a band of Reach, Possible or Strong beside the application, with the changes listed for the resume, cover letter and portfolio.
The panel file tells the agent not to rewrite the resume or the cover letter.

requirements.requirement: Render must show an application match check that marks each requirement of a posting as met, partly met or missing.

Each requirement carries exactly one of the three marks.
The check shows no single numeric score in place of the marks.

requirements.requirement: Render must build every agent from the same five parts and show the agent file assembling as the student answers.
done_when: Each agent step groups its questions under role, context, task, rules and handoff.
Typing an answer updates the agent file shown beside the questions.
The workshop shows six steps across the top in the order given in section 4.9.
After the student switches a file to hand editing, the copied and downloaded file contains the student’s own wording.

requirements.requirement: Render must read the exact headings in a pasted agent reply and route the results to the job log, the application and the gap list.
done_when: A pasted job search reply adds its openings to the job log.
A pasted panel reply shows the odds and the changes beside that job’s application.
Gaps from any reply appear in one gap list that is visible on every step.
A gap returned by more than one agent shows a count above one.

The portfolio link entered in the dashboard appears in the workshop.

Prompts copied from Render contain no name, address, phone number or email.

The tester saves a goal, closes the browser, reopens Render on the same computer and sees the goal.
The tester uses Save to File, opens Render on a second computer, uses Load from File and sees the same work.
With the network inspector open, saving a goal or a resume draft sends nothing to any server.

The tester signs in on a second device with the same handle and PIN and sees the same work.
The stored record holds the handle and the student's career content and no field that names the student.
The backend account is owned by the district or the department, and the district has approved it for student work.

requirements.requirement: The Syllabus Checker must run as Google Apps Script bound to the department’s existing Google Form and start on each form submission.
done_when: Submitting the form starts one run of the script with no manual step.
The project has an onFormSubmit trigger and no polling or time-based trigger for the check.
The script is owned by the department account and not by a personal account.

requirements.area: The approved language is read live, never copied
requirements.requirement: The Syllabus Checker must read the approved-language document on every run and keep no copy of it.
done_when: After the approved wording is edited in the reference document, the next submission is checked against the new wording with no change to the script.
No approved wording is found in the script source, in script properties or in the response sheet.

requirements.requirement: The Syllabus Checker must normalize both the approved text and the syllabus text before any comparison.
done_when: A syllabus that contains the approved statement with curly quotes or a curly apostrophe passes.
A syllabus that contains the approved statement with long dashes in place of hyphens passes.
A syllabus that contains the approved statement with extra spaces, line breaks or different capitalization passes.

requirements.requirement: The Syllabus Checker must check that the approved seat-hours statement appears verbatim in the syllabus.
done_when: A syllabus containing the exact approved statement is reported as having it.

The check gives the same result with the model turned off.

requirements.requirement: The Syllabus Checker must check for the RSI statement by fingerprint phrase only when the course is online or hybrid.

When modality is unknown, the report makes no pass or fail claim about the RSI statement.

requirements.requirement: The Syllabus Checker must flag a section marked combined that lists no associated class numbers.
done_when: A submission marked combined with no associated class numbers is flagged.
A submission marked combined with associated class numbers listed is not flagged.
A submission not marked combined is not flagged.

requirements.requirement: The Syllabus Checker must validate each class number against the pattern PREFIX###-#####.
done_when: A class number of three letters, three digits, a hyphen and five digits passes.

requirements.requirement: The Syllabus Checker must compute the submission deadline as the Friday of the first week from the class start date.

The literal checks give the same result with the model turned off.

requirements.requirement: The Syllabus Checker must send the ambiguous Reg 3.6 elements to a model only when that option is enabled, and must label every model finding as a suggestion.
done_when: In the default configuration no request leaves the Google tenant.
With the option enabled, every model finding in the report is labeled as a suggestion and none is reported as a failure.
With the option enabled, the text sent to the model does not include the instructor name or email taken from the form.
Changing the model provider requires a change to one function only.

questions: Now that the tool is in use, are faculty emails on, was the shadow-mode term run and the bar met, and are the fuzzy Reg 3.6 checks enabled and with which model?
What is the full list of Reg 3.6 elements, which are literal with which keywords and which are fuzzy, and can a model suggestion ever change a report from complete to incomplete?
How is modality determined today, and how does the script pick the right seat-hours statement from the approved-language document for a given course?
For the deadline check, what is compared against the computed Friday and what does the report say when a submission is late; and what are the allowed status values and their colors?
Is the weekly digest built, who receives it and what runs it; and should instructor names and emails that appear inside the syllabus text be removed before a model call?

1. Summary: Faculty submit a syllabus, it is checked against MCCCD and program requirements, the instructor gets an itemized reply within seconds, and every submission is logged in one place.
The tool is read-only. It reports, it never revises. No instructor should discover that an automated process quietly rewrote a document they are accountable for.

The check logic and interface were built in June: the deterministic checks, the live approved-language read, normalization, the faculty email report, and the response-sheet status columns. The author has confirmed that the tool is in use.
2. Goal: Move syllabus compliance from a manual, end-of-review bottleneck to an instant, consistent check that runs at the moment of submission. The reason this matters is pedagogical before it is administrative. A complete, consistent, accessible syllabus is the first thing a student reads and the document they return to all term: it sets the expectations, names the support services, and carries the accommodation and response-time language that students who need it most depend on. When a required statement is missing or a deadline is unclear, the cost lands on the student as confusion, and on the faculty member as the emails and appeals that follow. Catching gaps before the term starts, rather than in week six when a problem surfaces, keeps the syllabus doing its job.

Two concrete outcomes follow. The instructor learns what is missing in seconds instead of weeks, with the correct approved wording supplied so there is nothing to go find, and the department sees the status of every section in one sortable place without opening a single attachment. The review it replaces is slow, its consistency depends on who is doing it, and it produces no single view of who has complied.
3. Users and context: - Need: to know what is missing and fix it without hunting for the approved wording.
- What they receive: an email within seconds naming each gap, with the correct approved language supplied inline, ready to paste.
- Need: to monitor compliance across every section of the term.
- What they receive: status columns written back into the response spreadsheet they already own. One sortable log, not a forty-report inbox.

The split between those two outputs is the central design decision, and it is what keeps the tool serving people rather than burying them. Faculty need to act, so they get a message they can act on. The administrator needs to see the whole term, so she gets a log. Sending the administrator a copy of every individual report is not monitoring, it is drowning, and it is the mistake most compliance tools make.

The department already collects syllabi through a Google Form on a college Workspace account, so faculty habit does not change, and the seat-hour profiles are currently written for the college Art and Humanities.
4. How it works: Faculty submit through the existing Google Form. An onFormSubmit trigger fires inside the department’s Workspace, the script reads the approved-language document live and extracts the submitted syllabus text, normalizes and compares the two, emails the instructor the itemized report, and writes status columns back to the response sheet. Two design choices carry most of the trust.
### The approved language is read live, never copied

The script reads the reference document on every run and stores no copy. A stale stored copy is how compliance checklists fail: the department revises the wording, nobody updates the checker, and the tool starts approving syllabi against language that is no longer current. Reading live means the check is correct the same minute the source document changes, and there is nothing to maintain.

Whether an approved statement appears verbatim is a string comparison, not a judgment call. A language model would be worse at it, because it might decide a paraphrase counts as a match, and on text an accreditor reads, a confident wrong answer is the worst possible outcome. So the model is reserved for the ambiguous Reg 3.6 elements and clearly labeled as a suggestion, and the tool delivers most of its value with the model turned off.

Before any comparison, both texts are normalized (curly quotes to straight, dashes to hyphens, whitespace collapsed, case lowered), because a verbatim check that fails on a curly apostrophe is useless and formatting noise must never produce a false failure.
- Approved seat-hours statement: verbatim string comparison against the live document, after normalization. Uses AI: no.
- RSI statement (online and hybrid only): fingerprint phrase match, conditional on modality, never asserted when modality is unknown. Uses AI: no.
- Combined-section integrity: flags a section marked combined with no associated class numbers listed. Uses AI: no.
- Class-number format: regex against PREFIX###-#####. Uses AI: no.
- Submission deadline: computed from the class start date, the Friday of the first week. Uses AI: no.
- MCCCD Reg 3.6 elements (Title IX, accommodations, response time, and similar): keyword match for the literal ones, a model for the fuzzy ones. Uses AI: partly.
### Reading the syllabus, and its limit

Google Docs are read natively through DocumentApp, and Word files are converted through Drive and the temporary copy discarded. PDF text extraction is imperfect, and a verbatim check against imperfectly extracted text produces false failures, so when a submission is a PDF the report says plainly that extraction may be unreliable and tells the instructor to resubmit as a document if it flags language they know is present. The tool never fails anyone silently.
Syllabus+ PDF URLs are accepted by the form but not yet followed.
- To the instructor: an email, complete or incomplete, with each finding named and the approved wording supplied where relevant.
- To the department: four columns written into the existing response sheet (check status, missing items, file type, date checked), with the status cell colored by state in solid colors.
- Optional weekly digest of what is still outstanding.
5. Data, privacy, and governance: A syllabus is instructor content, not student content. It is a course document written by the faculty member and distributed to a class, containing no grades, no enrollment records, no submissions, and no student identifiers, so no FERPA-protected record is created, transmitted, or stored anywhere in this workflow. The system never touches a student record and has no path to one.
There is no database, no logging, and no analytics. The only things written anywhere are a status value in a spreadsheet the department already owns and an email to the person who submitted.
Everything runs inside the district’s own Google tenant, and the default configuration uses no AI, so nothing is sent to an external service.

If the optional fuzzy Reg 3.6 checks are enabled, the only text sent to a model is syllabus prose written by the instructor; the instructor’s name and email stay in the Workspace layer and are never included in a model call. If the district prefers that no content leave the tenant at all, the fuzzy checks turn off and the deterministic checks still run.
The script is read-only, with no write access to any submitted syllabus, and it is owned by the department account rather than a personal one, so it survives staff turnover.
6. Build and portability: The tool is Google Apps Script bound to the department’s existing Google Form, triggered by onFormSubmit with no polling or scheduler. Its source of truth is the department’s approved-language Google Doc read live on every run, it logs to the form’s own Google Sheet, and it notifies through Gmail, all on the college Workspace account. A static HTML page on GitHub Pages demonstrates the workflow; the working system runs in Workspace.

Apps Script is the right runtime because the department already lives in Google Workspace: the script runs there as an authorized user with access to Docs, Drive, Sheets, and Gmail already granted, so there is no OAuth consent screen to publish, no client secret to protect, no server to host, no CORS proxy, and no vendor. It already runs on district infrastructure, under accounts, permissions, and audit logging that OIT administers, so installation is an administrative authorization on the department account, not a deployment.

The optional AI call sits behind one interface, text in and findings out, so nothing else depends on which model answers. It can point at Claude, at Gemini (already inside the Workspace tenant and the lowest-friction option for a district that wants no traffic leaving Google), or at a district-hosted endpoint, and swapping providers changes one function rather than the tool. Because the deterministic checks carry most of the value, the system runs correctly with no model at all.

Serving more than one department is configuration, not a rebuild: each supplies its own form, approved-language document, and department account, while the district-wide Reg 3.6 elements are the portable core and need no work. There is no multi-tenant version and none is planned, because ten small scripts each department owns fit how these forms are actually administered better than one central system nobody owns.
7. Pilot and testing: The intended way to earn trust before anyone relies on it is a shadow-mode term: run the checker on every syllabus submitted through the existing form in one department, log the results, and send no faculty email, while the manual review continues in parallel as the system of record.

The point is to compare the checker against the human reviewer and count false failures (flagging language that is present) separately from misses (passing a syllabus that is missing something), since a false failure destroys trust fastest.
Disagreement on the AI-assisted fuzzy elements is expected, which is exactly why they are labeled suggestions and never failures.
The tool is now in use. The document does not record whether the shadow-mode term was run or what it found.
8. Definition of success: - Zero false failures and zero misses on the deterministic checks against Google Doc and Word submissions, because those are string comparisons and anything above zero is a bug rather than a tolerance.
- A clear reduction in the reviewer’s manual verbatim-checking time, reported by the person doing it.
- Faculty who can act on the report without asking what it means.
- Every unreadable file reported as unreadable rather than guessed.

The outcomes it serves are the two named in the goal: the instructor learns what is missing in seconds instead of weeks, and the department sees the status of every section in one sortable place without opening a single attachment.
9. Rollout: The tool is in use, bound to the department’s existing Google Form on the college Workspace account. Nothing runs until the account that owns the form authorizes the script, so installation is an administrative authorization on the department account, not a deployment.

The planned sequence is that faculty email turns on only after the shadow-mode term meets the bar, with the manual review kept as a backstop for one more term. The document does not record which of these steps are complete.

Any offer to a second department or another college would be configuration taken one step at a time, with OIT and the ARC asked to review the AI configuration and put the data boundary in writing first.
10. Open questions and risks: - PDF extraction. PDF text extraction is imperfect, and a verbatim check against imperfectly extracted text produces false failures. The durable fix is policy rather than code: ask the department to accept Google Docs and Word.
- Form field matching. Form fields are matched by exact title, so a reworded question currently makes the script read nothing.
- Modality. RSI applicability is inferred, because the form has no modality question.
- Syllabus+ PDF URLs are accepted by the form but not yet followed; that needs a fetch-and-parse step and inherits the same extraction limit.
- False failures. A false failure destroys trust fastest.
- Data boundary. If the district prefers that no content leave the tenant at all, the fuzzy checks turn off and the deterministic checks still run.
11. Roadmap: The known fragilities to fix before it travels:
- Match form fields by ID rather than exact title.
- Add a modality question so RSI applicability is asked rather than inferred.
Also named in the document, with no order or timing given:
- A fetch-and-parse step so Syllabus+ PDF URLs are followed.
- An offer to a second department or another college, as configuration, after OIT and the ARC review the AI configuration and put the data boundary in writing.
There is no multi-tenant version and none is planned.
